topic: The Additive Property of Normal Distributions: Gaussian + Gaussian = Gaussian
target_audience: University students (Statistics, Engineering, or Data Science)

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1 min)
lecture_lines: Normal distributions follow the bell curve shape.
Random variables have defined mean and variance.
Independent variables means errors don't influence each other.
animations: Create a title text 'Combinatorics Basics' in #FFFFFF at center.

sections.title: The Rule of Summation (1.5 min)
lecture_lines: Adding two normal variables is a new normal.
The mean of the sum is the sum of means.
The variance of the sum is the sum of variances.
The combined distribution is a new bell curve.
This rule applies to all independent Gaussian distributions.
animations: Display the formula 'Sum = A + B' in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Why' (1.5 min)
lecture_lines: Two narrow distributions represent specific uncertainties.
Adding them shifts the mean to the right.
The final curve is wider due to added variance.
This visual superposition confirms the rule of summation.
Uncertainty grows as we combine independent processes.

sections.title: Real-world Application & Summary (1 min)
lecture_lines: Total delivery time is a simple Gaussian sum.
Complex systems become predictable with this arithmetic.
Predictable outcomes simplify real-world data modeling.
